packages.label: תּוֹרָה וּמַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי
packages.label_en: Torah and Making the Simple Wise
packages.reason: This cluster groups all concepts that share the essential nature of Torah as the faithful witness and maker of wisdom in the hidden domain. The teaching's core bechina declarations define this package: (1) Torah IS CALLED (הַנִּקְרֵאת) a woman — an אִשָּׁה — which is why she can testify in the place where men are not accustomed to be; (2) 'הַחֲרָטָה, זֶה בְּחִינַת מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי' — the regret after a transgression IS a bechina of 'making the simple wise.' These two bechina statements link five concepts into a single nature-family: Torah is the woman who stands in the secret place (the locus of lust) and whose calling elicits wisdom-regret from the transgressor. Torah, her identity as אִשָּׁה, her function as עֵדוּת (testimony), the capacity of מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי (making the peti wise), and the concrete result חֲרָטָה (regret after the transgression) all share the same essential domain: the redemptive power of Torah that reaches the sinner even in the hidden world of desire. These are not cause-and-effect (the regret is not produced by Torah in an eitza sense within this package — rather, the regret IS the בחינת of the Torah's making-wise action, i.e., they are the same thing seen from different angles). Polarity is good: this cluster belongs entirely to the domain of holiness, Torah, and spiritual recovery.

packages.label: תַּאֲווֹת וְרוּחַ שְׁטוּת
packages.label_en: Lusts and the Spirit of Folly
packages.reason: This cluster groups all concepts that share the essential nature of the hidden domain of lust and spiritual folly — the realm that Torah must penetrate to testify. The teaching's two bechina statements for this package are: (1) 'עִקַּר תַּאֲווֹת הֵם בַּסֵּתֶר, בִּבְחִינַת מַיִם גְּנוּבִים יִמְתָּקוּ' — the essential nature of lusts operating in secret IS (בְּחִינַת) 'stolen waters are sweet' (Prov. 9:17); (2) 'כִּי בִּשְׁעַת הָעֲבֵרָה הָיָה בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת' — at the moment of the transgression, the spirit of folly inhabits him [implied IS-equation between the sinner's state and ruach shtut, grounded in the Talmudic dictum of Sota 3a: 'ein adam over aveira ela im ken nikhnas bo ruach shtut']. The four concepts in this package — תַּאֲווֹת (lusts), מַיִם גְּנוּבִים (stolen waters), הַסֵּתֶר (the hidden/secret domain), and רוּחַ שְׁטוּת (spirit of folly) — all share the same essential domain: the hidden world of desire, sin, and spiritual blindness that is the antithesis of Torah wisdom. The connection between them is one of shared essential nature, not cause-and-effect: lust IS the stolen-waters quality; the secret-hiding IS where lust lives; the ruach shtut IS the inner state of the person in the moment of lust-driven transgression. The concept עֲבֵרָה (transgression) belongs here because the Rebbe explicitly defines it as the moment of ruach shtut — the transgression IS the ruach-shtut event. All four form a single bechina-family of the evil pole. Polarity is evil: this cluster belongs to the domain of the sitra achra, desire, and spiritual folly.
